sections.h2: Which Franklin County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
The Franklin County Tax Office has three departments: the Assessor's Office, the Collections Department and GIS/Mapping. The office phone is 919-496-2172, and callers may reach voicemail when volume is heavy.

The assessor lists, appraises and values real estate, personal property and registered motor vehicles. The collector, who works under the North Carolina Machinery Act, collects current and delinquent tax. Mail for value questions goes to the Tax Assessor's Office, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549, and mail for payments or certifications goes to the Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549.

Franklin County has grown fast, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate of 82,037 residents is 19.5 percent above the 2020 base of 68,625. It covers 491.80 square miles of land, with 139.4 people per square mile in 2020. The 2020 to 2024 survey shows 78.6 percent owner-occupancy, a median owner-occupied value of $284,300 and a mean commute of 33.3 minutes.

sections.h2: When are Franklin County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes for the year are due September 1 and become delinquent after January 5, and the 2026 bills turn delinquent on January 6, 2027.

The county sends bills in late July or early August. An owner who pays before September 1 can receive a discount, and prepayments are possible before the bills are produced. After the delinquency date the county uses enforced collection, and state interest of 2 percent from January 6 to February 1 and three-fourths of one percent per month after that applies (G.S. 105-360).

Paying is possible by phone or online. Credit cards go through a third party, BIS Online Services, which charges a non-refundable convenience fee, and the phone line is 877-768-4775. A caller needs the tax year, bill number, local zip code and amount, and the county office at 919-496-2172 can supply the correct figure. Past-due notices sometimes cross with a payment, so pay before the delinquent date and include accrued interest if you are late.

sections.h2: Why do I get a bill if my mortgage lender pays the tax?
sections.html:
The county mails the bill to the owner of record even when a lender escrows the tax, because the lender selects the bills it will pay from a county file.

To confirm the lender paid, check the county's collection search in the second week of September, or call 919-496-2172 and choose option 2. Sending a copy of the bill to the mortgage company with the next house payment is the county's own suggestion. If you sold the house, forward the bill to the new owner unless you intend to pay it. The county says agreements among buyers, sellers and attorneys are not its concern, but the tax is a lien on real estate, so a buyer should see every bill settled before closing.

sections.h2: What is the tax certification on a Franklin County deed?
sections.html:
Since April 1, 2015, the Franklin County Register of Deeds will not accept a deed transferring real property unless the Tax Collector has certified that no delinquent tax is a lien on it.

The Collections Department provides the certification free on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., excluding county holidays, so a closing attorney or seller can stop by before recording. Mail requests go to the Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, marked Attention: Tax Certification. Electronic recording routes the deed through the certification step automatically.

For a seller, that means an unpaid bill can stall the recording of the deed. If the current bill is open, pay it or arrange for the closing agent to pay it from proceeds so the certification can be issued.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Franklin County value?
sections.html:
File a real estate appeal after January 1 and before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, which is usually in May, or within 30 days of any value change notice.

The current revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, so values are measured as of that date. The county asks owners to send its appeal form with all supporting papers to Franklin County Revaluation, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549, before April. If staff review does not settle the matter, the board schedules a hearing and mails its decision. An appeal filed after adjournment is heard the next tax year. The owner can then go to the North Carolina Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the board's notice, and the owner carries the burden of proof that the value is substantially overstated.

Reasons the Franklin County Tax Office says do or do not support a reduction (source: county Value Appeals page)
Reason offeredCounty position
The bill is higher than last year, or you are retired on a fixed incomeNo legal basis
Values fell, or you paid less, after January 1, 2024No legal basis under G.S. 105-287
Similar properties carry lower assessed valuesHas a legal basis
Sales of highly similar properties before January 1, 2024 at much lower pricesHas a legal basis

sections.h2: What tax relief can Franklin County owners claim?
sections.html:
The same three state programs apply: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker, and an owner may use only one of them.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, income limit $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax capped at 4 percent of income up to $38,800 and 5 percent up to $58,200 for owners who have lived in the home five years, with the excess deferred.

Apply on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, not the state revenue department. The county's appeals page points retirees on a fixed income to the Tax Assessor's Office for relief eligibility, since a fixed income is not a reason to lower the value. If an owner sells, the circuit breaker deferral comes due.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Franklin County fees and liens?
sections.html:
Franklin County adds a solid waste availability fee to bills for dwellings and businesses with an electrical hookup or meter, and the tax itself is a lien on the parcel.

The county explains that the fee pays for collection and disposal at twelve convenience centers, applies per electrical connection and does not require full-time residence, so a vacant house with power still carries it. Commissioners set the amount each year in the budget ordinance, so ask the Tax Office for the current figure on your parcel.

If a bill goes unpaid, G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien as of the listing date and G.S. 105-374 lets the county foreclose it in court, with a courthouse-door sale and a 10-day window for increased bids. An owner who files bankruptcy still receives bills, though the collector cannot pursue delinquent tax during the case.

faqs.q: When do Franklin County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They become delinquent after January 5 of the year following the September 1 due date. The county states that 2026 bills become delinquent on January 6, 2027.

faqs.q: Does Franklin County require tax certification before recording a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register of Deeds will not accept a deed transferring real property unless the Tax Collector certifies there is no delinquent tax lien. The certification is free on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Franklin County assessment?
faqs.a: Send the Board of Equalization and Review appeal form with supporting papers to P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549. File after January 1 and before adjournment, usually in May, or within 30 days of a value change notice.

faqs.q: Is a high tax bill a reason to lower my Franklin County value?
faqs.a: No. The county lists a higher bill or a fixed income as having no legal basis. Better evidence is a comparison with similar properties, pre-2024 sales of highly similar properties or documented damage.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Franklin County tax payment?
faqs.a: Call 919-496-2172, and choose option 2 to check whether taxes are paid. Credit card payments by phone go through BIS Online Services at 877-768-4775, and a convenience fee applies.
